newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to stay at home of wealthy contributor.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to stay at home of wealthy contributor.

text.p: When President Bill Clinton goes to Martha's Vineyard on vacation on Sunday, he will be staying at the home of a wealthy Boston developer who has a couple of projects that require federal approval.
The White House was quick to deny on Thursday that there was anything wrong with the arrangement of Clinton accepting free lodging from the developer, Richard Friedman.
Friedman has a 20-acre estate in the Oyster Pond area of the Massachusetts resort island. Clinton stayed there during his 1994 vacation as well.

"Just because someone has some issue pending with the federal government doesn't rule them out as someone who can grant an act of hospitality to the president of the United States," said White House spokesman Mike McCurry.
Friedman has two projects whose success depends on federal approval, a hotel on Boston's City Hall Plaza and a bingo hall in Fall River, Mass.
The General Services Administration is opposing Friedman's development team's plans for a 350-room hotel at City Hall Plaza.
Asked whether there was a conflict, McCurry told reporters: "As far as I know, this matter was reviewed and vetted by counsel."
"Mr. Friedman has indicated to the White House that he's never had any contact with the White House pending on any of the matters that have gotten any potential federal involvement," he said.
The Boston Herald quoted real estate sources as saying the value of the lodging for the president and his family was estimated at $10,000 to $15,000.

It said Friedman was one of the Democratic contributors who stayed overnight in the White House Lincoln Bedroom during the fund-raising cycle for last year's presidential election campaign. The Clintons are scheduled to remain at Martha's Vineyard for three weeks.
McCurry said Clinton seems anxious to take his annual long break from Washington because he mentions it in "every other conversation you have with him."
